bio: My research began with molecular contacts and thin-film electrodes in organic and hybrid optoelectronics. First-author work now spans trap-controlled optoelectronic memory, hydrogen-bond-engineered artificial synapses, and chiral perovskite devices that store optical helicity as persistent analog conductance states.
vision: I study how interfaces, defects, and ionic dynamics shape memory-state formation and reliability. Work on printed stretchable interconnects adds a complementary foundation in process-induced electrical variability and mechanical reliability. My ongoing doctoral project examines multilevel ionic-memory precision; low-temperature integration and computing hardware remain future research directions.
